# aeo

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** technical-seo, on-page-seo, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** geo, copywriting, structured-data, web-analytics

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a page should be liftable by an answer engine — featured snippets, voice answers, Google AI Overviews / AI Mode — or when an AEO plan, tactic, or result is being written, reviewed, or reported.
- **Do NOT use when:** the problem is crawlability or indexation (use technical-seo), page intent and metadata (use on-page-seo), citation inside synthesized multi-source answers as a program (use geo), or markup implementation (use structured-data).

## Rules

1. **CO-041 — Answer first, self-contained.** The passage that answers the query sits at the top of its section and is true and complete when lifted alone: no "as mentioned above", no pronoun whose antecedent lives in another paragraph, no fact that needs the surrounding page to make sense.
2. **CO-042 — Question-shaped headings for question queries.** Where the target query is a question, the heading states that question in the searcher's wording and the answer passage follows it immediately; statements and procedures use descriptive headings instead.
3. **CO-043 — Extractable formats for extractable facts.** Procedural steps go in ordered lists, comparisons in tables, and definitions in a single sentence followed by expansion — formats that survive extraction intact.
4. **CO-044 — One canonical statement of every fact.** A fact used in an answer passage is stated once, in one canonical wording, and matches fact-sheet.md exactly; answer engines amplify contradictions, so a second wording of the same fact anywhere on the site is a defect (DET-CON-015 discipline).
5. **CO-045 — One version of the content.** The same page serves people and engines. No separate "AI version", no answer text hidden from users, no engine-only variant of a passage.
6. **CO-046 — AI-feature eligibility is ordinary Search eligibility (Documented).** For Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, a page must be indexed and eligible to appear in Search with a snippet; Google states there are no additional technical requirements, no special optimizations, and no special schema.org markup. Any plan claiming a further Google requirement must cite the Google page that states it.
7. **CO-047 — Every tactic carries an evidence-level tag.** Each AEO tactic in a plan, audit, or report is labeled Documented (platform-stated), Peer-reviewed (with the study's limits), Correlational (vendor/observational), or Hype (unsupported or contradicted). An untagged tactic fails review.
8. **CO-048 — llms.txt is hygiene, never a result (Hype if claimed otherwise).** llms.txt is a 2024 proposal, not an adopted standard; Google has stated on the record that it does not use the file, and a study of nearly 300,000 domains found no correlation with LLM citation frequency. The file may be shipped, but it is never reported as an AI-visibility win and never described as a Google-endorsed ranking factor.
9. **CO-049 — Crawler access is verified at every layer.** AI and search crawlers allowed in robots.txt must also pass the CDN, firewall, and hosting layer; Google's AI-features guidance names CDN/hosting blocking as a real eligibility failure, so access is tested with the crawler's user agent, not assumed.
10. **CO-050 — Answer-supporting structured data matches the visible text.** Any markup behind an answer (FAQ, HowTo, product facts) is generated from the same data as the rendered page and agrees with it field for field (DET-CON-024).
11. **CO-051 — Citability additions are sourced or absent (Peer-reviewed, limited).** Adding citations, quotations, and statistics is the one tactic with peer-reviewed support for raising visibility in generated answers (Aggarwal et al., KDD '24, GEO-bench, 2023-era models — an upper-bound result, not an average). Every added statistic or quotation must trace to a real source record under the real-content rule; an invented figure is a DET-CON-011 blocker even if it earns citations.
12. **CO-052 — Answer presence is measured on a fixed query set.** A written set of target queries is checked on a monthly cadence in AI Overviews and featured snippets, with date, engine, and citing URL logged. One screenshot of one answer is an anecdote, never a reported result.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-021 — llms.txt sold as a ranking factor.** Banned: presenting llms.txt (or any "AI text file") as a Google-endorsed ranking factor, a requirement for AI Overviews, or a measured visibility result. Defeats: DET-NONE — no DET parameter names this signal; governed by CO-048. Instead: ship the file as hygiene if wanted and report it as such, tagged Hype/contradicted per CO-048, citing Google's on-record statements. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-022 — Separate or hidden AI-only content.** Banned: an engine-facing version of a page, or answer passages hidden from users (display:none, off-screen, crawler-only rendering) that differ from what users read. Defeats: DET-CON-024. Instead: one page serves both — write the answer into the visible content (CO-045). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-023 — Fabricated citation bait.** Banned: inventing a statistic, quotation, or study result to make a passage more citable by answer engines. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: cite a real, producible source or delete the figure (CO-051). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-024 — Templated answer-page matrix.** Banned: stamping out one thin Q&A page per query variant with swapped keywords and no page-specific substance, to capture answer placements at scale. Defeats: DET-CON-025. Instead: one canonical answer page per topic, expanded only with verified page-specific material. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-025 — Contradictory canonical answers.** Banned: two pages (or a page and its markup) stating different values for the same fact an engine might lift — prices, limits, dates, counts. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: state the fact once, from fact-sheet.md, and link rather than restate (CO-044). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CO-021 — Evidence-tag audit.** Verifies: CO-047, CO-048. Check: manual review of the AEO plan/report — every tactic line carries one of the four evidence tags, and no llms.txt or "AI file" line is tagged Documented or reported as a result. Pass: 100% of tactics tagged, zero hype presented as fact. Fail: return the plan for re-tagging before any work ships.
- **G-CO-022 — Answer-presence log.** Verifies: CO-052. Check: monthly — run the fixed target-query set, record date, surface (AI Overview / featured snippet / none), and the citing URL in the log; compare against the previous month. Pass: log entry complete for every query in the set. Fail: the month's AEO reporting is marked unmeasured, not estimated.
- **G-CO-023 — Passage self-containment and fact diff.** Verifies: CO-041, CO-044. Check: automated assist — grep answer sections for cross-reference dependencies: `grep -rniE 'as mentioned above|see above|as noted earlier|the aforementioned' content/` returns nothing; then diff every checkable fact in answer passages against fact-sheet.md. Pass: zero cross-references, zero fact mismatches. Fail: rewrite the passage before release.
- **G-CO-024 — Crawler access test.** Verifies: CO-049. Check: automated — request key pages with the search crawler's user agent and assert a 200 with full content: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -A "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)" https://example.com/pricing` returns `200`, and robots.txt shows no Disallow for the path. Pass: 200 and no block at CDN, firewall, or robots layer. Fail: fix the blocking layer before claiming AEO eligibility.
- **G-CO-025 — Answer markup match.** Verifies: CO-050. Check: automated — parse each page's JSON-LD and diff answer-relevant fields (FAQ answers, prices, ratings) against the rendered text. Pass: every field has an identical visible counterpart. Fail: regenerate the markup from page data or remove it.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Each target passage answers its query in its first sentences and stands alone when lifted (CO-041, G-CO-023).
- [ ] Question headings match real queries; procedures and comparisons use lists and tables (CO-042, CO-043).
- [ ] Every fact in an answer passage matches fact-sheet.md, stated in one canonical wording (CO-044).
- [ ] No AI-only or hidden content variant exists (CO-045).
- [ ] Every tactic in the plan/report carries an evidence-level tag; llms.txt is not claimed as a result (CO-047, CO-048, G-CO-021).
- [ ] Crawler access verified at robots, CDN, and hosting layers (CO-049, G-CO-024).
- [ ] Answer-supporting structured data matches the visible text field for field (CO-050, G-CO-025).
- [ ] This month's fixed-query answer-presence log is complete (CO-052, G-CO-022).

# content-strategy

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** fact-sheet, web-analytics
- **Feeds into:** copywriting, on-page-seo, real-content, internal-linking

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** deciding what content a site will produce, in what order, for whom, and to what end — topic maps, editorial calendars, briefs, and refresh/retire decisions. This skill owns the production system: strategy sets audience, goals, and topic ownership before any drafting starts.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is how a single page is written (copywriting), how its metadata is set (on-page-seo), or whether a specific factual element is evidenced (real-content — that gate runs at publish time and its blocker list outranks any plan made here). Never use strategy to justify volume the evidence cannot support.

## Rules

1. **CO-081 — No brief, no draft.** Every piece of content starts from a brief naming its audience, goal, target query or intent, owner, and reviewer. A brief missing any of the five does not enter production, and no draft is written against an unwritten brief.
2. **CO-082 — Volume is an output, never a quota.** The plan never sets a pages-per-week or pages-per-month target. Output is whatever number of briefs clear the CO-081 bar; Google's scaled content abuse policy makes volume-for-rankings the violation regardless of whether humans or AI wrote the pages.
3. **CO-083 — One canonical page per topic.** The topic map assigns each topic to exactly one canonical page. A second page on the same topic is admitted only with a written differentiation: a different audience, format, or body of page-specific verified material the canonical page does not carry.
4. **CO-084 — The swap test for variants.** A location, keyword, or product variant page ships only with real page-specific data (staff, stock, pricing, regulations, local facts) such that swapping the keyword back would break the page. If two variants stay interchangeable after the swap, they are one page, not two.
5. **CO-085 — Every piece carries an owner and a review-by date.** At publication, each page records a named owner and the date by which its claims are re-verified. A page with no owner or no review-by date is not finished, however polished the copy.
6. **CO-086 — Authorship is real.** Pieces are credited to real people the publisher can evidence, or to an accountable house byline ("The Support Team"). Invented author personas — names, headshots, bios for people who do not exist — are never planned, briefed, or published.
7. **CO-087 — Decisions cite data.** Every brief, refresh, and retirement names the evidence behind it: Search Console query/page data, analytics landing-page evidence, or a documented audience need. "We should write about X" with no cited evidence is an opinion, and opinions do not enter the calendar.
8. **CO-088 — Topics stay inside the real offer.** The topic map covers only subjects the business can actually serve and evidence from its own operation. A topic the business has no product, service, data, or experience behind is out of scope, however much search demand it shows.
9. **CO-089 — Refresh or retire on schedule.** When a page's review-by date arrives, its owner re-verifies its claims and then refreshes, retires, or re-dates it with the verification recorded. Silently editing the date without re-verifying the content is not a refresh.
10. **CO-090 — The programmatic admission bar.** Templated or programmatic page sets are admitted only when every page in the set carries page-specific verified data passing CO-084. A set whose pages differ only in a swapped term is rejected at planning, not discovered at audit.
11. **CO-091 — Distribution is part of the brief.** A brief is incomplete until it names the page's planned inbound internal links and its distribution step (newsletter, social, partner, in-product). A page planned to be found "by the sitemap" is planned to be orphaned.
12. **CO-092 — Depth per topic over page count.** When a topic cannot support another substantively different page, the plan deepens the canonical page — new verified data, better coverage of the intent — instead of spawning a sibling. The plan records this choice so the refusal of volume is a decision on file, not an omission.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-041 — Volume-quota planning.** Banned: setting a content target in pages per week/month, or back-filling a calendar to hit a count. Defeats: DET-CON-025. Instead: plan briefs that clear CO-081 and let the count be whatever survives; depth per topic (CO-092) absorbs the remaining effort. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-042 — Template-stamped page sets.** Banned: approving a set of pages built from one skeleton with keywords swapped per page. Defeats: DET-CON-008. Instead: admit only variants carrying real local data that passes the swap test (CO-084); merge the rest into one canonical page (CO-083). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-043 — Invented author personas.** Banned: creating fictional writers — name, headshot, bio, credentials — to make the content program look staffed. Defeats: DET-CON-020. Instead: credit real people with an author page and an independent trace, or use an honestly collective house byline (CO-086). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-044 — Expired claims left live by default.** Banned: letting dated copy (sale banners, "new for 2024", registration for past events) stay published past its date with no owner action. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: every dated claim carries an owner and review-by date (CO-085) and is refreshed or retired on schedule (CO-089). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CO-041 — Brief traceability audit.** Verifies: CO-081, CO-087. Check: automated — diff the published URL inventory against the brief register; every published URL must map to a brief containing audience, goal, intent, owner, reviewer, and a cited evidence source. Pass: 100% of published URLs trace to a complete brief. Fail: unbriefed pages are pulled from the calendar owner's queue and briefed retroactively or unpublished.
- **G-CO-042 — Corpus similarity clustering.** Verifies: CO-083, CO-084, CO-090. Check: automated — cluster published pages by text similarity; for every cluster of more than three pages, apply the swap test to a sample pair. Pass: no cluster whose sampled pages are interchangeable after keyword swap. Fail: the set is merged to its canonical page or each page is rebuilt with verified page-specific data before the next release.
- **G-CO-043 — Stale-date and review-by scan.** Verifies: CO-085, CO-089. Check: automated — extract date-bearing claims from published copy and diff the page inventory against the review-by register; flag any page past its review-by date and any claim asserting a past event as current. Pass: zero overdue pages and zero expired claims live. Fail: flagged pages are refreshed, retired, or re-dated with verification recorded before the next publish.
- **G-CO-044 — Authorship audit.** Verifies: CO-086. Check: manual — list every byline on the site; for each individual byline, require an author page plus one independent trace (staff page, professional profile); house bylines must name an accountable team, not a fake individual. Pass: every byline resolves to a real person or an honest collective. Fail: block publication under that byline until it does.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Every item in production traces to a brief with audience, goal, intent, owner, and reviewer (G-CO-041).
- [ ] The plan states no pages-per-week or pages-per-month target anywhere (CO-082).
- [ ] Each topic maps to one canonical page; variants carry a written differentiation (CO-083).
- [ ] Every variant page passes the swap test with real page-specific data (CO-084).
- [ ] Every published page has a named owner and a review-by date (CO-085).
- [ ] All bylines are real people or an accountable house byline (G-CO-044).
- [ ] Each brief, refresh, and retirement cites the data behind it (CO-087).
- [ ] Similarity clustering shows no interchangeable page set (G-CO-042).

# copywriting

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** fact-sheet, real-content
- **Feeds into:** on-page-seo, lifecycle-email, social-open-graph, structured-data

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** Writing or editing any user-facing copy — landing pages, product pages, blog posts, metadata, alt text, captions, email and ad copy.
- **Do NOT use when:** The task is verifying whether a factual element may exist at all (that is real-content's gate; copywriting consumes its verdicts), setting topic inventory (content-strategy), or writing documentation (D10 owns documentation-writing; the voice guide is shared, not duplicated).

## Rules

1. **CO-101 — Competitor-verbatim test.** Every benefit sentence must name a mechanism, a user, or a verifiable outcome specific to this product. If a competitor could print the sentence unchanged, rewrite it with a product-specific fact from fact-sheet.md or delete it. (DET-CON-006)
2. **CO-102 — Fact-sheet traceability.** Every factual claim in copy — feature, number, price, name, outcome — traces to an entry in fact-sheet.md or a source record the business can produce. A claim with no trace is cut, never softened into vagueness.
3. **CO-103 — Cluster-term editing pass.** Before shipping, search the draft for model-default vocabulary clusters (delve, tapestry, realm, furthermore, moreover, "it's important to note", "in today's fast-paced world") and rewrite each hit in the house voice. Co-occurrence of several cluster terms on one page is a defect, not a style choice. (DET-CON-007)
4. **CO-104 — One qualifier maximum.** A product claim carries at most one honest qualifier. Three or more qualifiers stacked on one claim ("may potentially help to possibly improve") mean the claim is unverified: verify it and state it plainly, or cut it. (DET-CON-009)
5. **CO-105 — Measurable superlatives need substantiation.** "#1", "best-rated", "largest", and any rank, share, or rated-position claim require substantiation on file (ranking, survey, or criteria) before use; without it, rewrite as plain description. Unmeasurable puffery is a style note, not a finding. (DET-CON-026)
6. **CO-106 — No invented numbers.** Every statistic, percentage, rating, and count in copy cites its source or dataset, and one canonical figure is used site-wide. Third-party claims (ratings, market share, comparisons) need provenance somewhere on the domain; first-party counters need a fact-sheet entry. (DET-CON-011)
7. **CO-107 — No invented social proof.** Testimonials, review quotes, and endorsements are used only when a producible source record exists (signed quote, review-platform link, customer email) and permission is held. No record, no quote — the section ships empty or not at all. (DET-CON-010)
8. **CO-108 — Naming list is exact.** Company, product, feature, plan, and people names are copied from the project's naming list character-for-character — capitalization, spacing, and spelling — on every surface. Never re-type a name from memory. (DET-CON-017)
9. **CO-109 — Alt text from the rendered image.** Alt text and captions describe the actual rendered image: what a sighted reader sees. Never write them from the filename, a keyword list, or the prompt that generated the image. Decorative images get `alt=""`, not a description. (DET-CON-027)
10. **CO-110 — Structure follows the material.** Page structure — headings, paragraph order, length — varies with the subject. Never stamp one skeleton across pages with only keywords swapped; if two drafts share a heading sequence, rewrite one from its own brief. (DET-CON-008)
11. **CO-111 — Promises need backing.** A present-tense operational promise ("24/7 support", "money-back guarantee", "cancel anytime") appears in copy only when the policy page or documented process that makes it true exists and is linked. No backing artifact, no promise. (DET-CON-028)
12. **CO-112 — People-first, metadata last.** Copy is written to help the named reader complete a task, in the house voice guide's register; titles and descriptions are written after the page is finished, from what the page actually delivers. (Google people-first guidance)

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-051 — Invented testimonial.** Banned: a quoted endorsement from a person whose source record the business cannot produce. Defeats: DET-CON-010. Instead: use only a quote with a signed or platform-verifiable source record and permission, or ship the section without testimonials. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-052 — Unsourced statistic.** Banned: a precise figure (percentage, rating, user count, comparison) with no source, dataset, or fact-sheet entry behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: cite the dataset the figure came from and record it in fact-sheet.md, or delete the number and describe the mechanism. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-053 — Unsubstantiated measurable superlative.** Banned: a rank or rated-position claim ("#1", "best-rated", "the leading provider") with no ranking, survey, or criteria on file. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Instead: name the comparison set and source ("Top-rated in the 2026 Remote Work Tools survey, n=412"), or write a plain description of what the product does. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-054 — Competitor-verbatim benefit filler.** Banned: a benefit sentence any competitor could print unchanged, with no product-specific fact attached. Defeats: DET-CON-006. Instead: name the mechanism and outcome — "Comments resolve into tasks with one click, so decisions stop getting lost in threads." Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-CO-055 — Hedge stack.** Banned: three or more qualifiers protecting a single product claim. Defeats: DET-CON-009. Instead: verify and commit — "TaskBoard tracks every task's owner and due date in one board" — or cut the claim. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CO-051 — Pre-publish lint (automated).** Verifies: CO-103, CO-104. Check: run `grep -rniE "delve|tapestry|realm|furthermore|moreover|it's important to note|in today's fast-paced world" <copy files>` and a qualifier-cluster scan for `may|might|can` within five words of `potentially|possibly|generally`; every hit is listed for the editor. Pass: zero unrewritten hits. Fail: block shipment until the editor rewrites or justifies each hit in progress.md.
- **G-CO-052 — Substantiation spot-check (manual).** Verifies: CO-102, CO-105, CO-106, CO-107. Check: list every measurable claim, statistic, superlative, and testimonial in the piece; trace each to its fact-sheet entry or source record. Pass: 100% traced. Fail: block shipment; untraced items are cut, not footnoted.
- **G-CO-053 — Naming lint (automated).** Verifies: CO-108. Check: extract proper nouns from the copy and diff against the naming list; flag every variant form of a listed entity. Pass: exactly one live form per entity. Fail: block shipment until variants are corrected.
- **G-CO-054 — Competitor-verbatim review (manual).** Verifies: CO-101, CO-110. Check: highlight every benefit sentence and ask "could a competitor print this verbatim?"; on interior pages flag any yes with no specific within one sentence either side, on heroes judge the page as a whole; compare heading sequences against two sibling pages. Pass: no flagged sentence survives and no shared skeleton. Fail: warn and rewrite before publish.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Every benefit sentence passes the competitor-verbatim test (CO-101).
- [ ] Every factual claim traces to fact-sheet.md or a source record (CO-102).
- [ ] Cluster-term and hedge lint run; all hits rewritten (CO-103, CO-104, G-CO-051).
- [ ] Every superlative and statistic has substantiation on file (CO-105, CO-106, G-CO-052).
- [ ] Every testimonial has a producible source record and permission (CO-107).
- [ ] All names match the naming list exactly (CO-108, G-CO-053).
- [ ] Alt text and captions written from the rendered images (CO-109).
- [ ] Every operational promise links to its backing policy or process (CO-111).

# geo

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** technical-seo, on-page-seo, aeo, real-content, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** web-analytics, content-strategy

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** planning, executing, or reporting work aimed at inclusion and citation inside synthesized answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Google AI Overviews / AI Mode) — building citable content, aligning brand facts across sources, or measuring citation presence over time.
- **Do NOT use when:** the target is a ranked position, featured snippet, or AI Overview eligibility on Google Search itself (use aeo and technical-seo), when the deliverable is ordinary page copy (use copywriting), or when a claim's evidence is in dispute — resolve it under real-content first.

## Rules

1. **CO-061 — Every GEO claim carries an evidence tag.** Each tactic or claim in a GEO plan or report is labeled documented (platform-stated), peer-reviewed, correlational (vendor/observational), or hype (contradicted or unsupported); an untagged claim fails review.
2. **CO-062 — Documented layer first.** Before any GEO tactic is planned, the site meets Google's stated AI-features fundamentals: indexed and snippet-eligible, crawling allowed including at CDN/hosting level, important content in textual form and findable through internal links, structured data matching visible text.
3. **CO-063 — No special files, markup, or scores are requirements.** No plan presents llms.txt, a special schema type, a machine-readable AI file, or a paid "GEO score" as a platform requirement or platform metric — Google states none exist.
4. **CO-064 — llms.txt is hygiene, never a result.** llms.txt may be shipped as harmless hygiene; it is never reported as an AI-visibility win, because Google has stated on the record that it does not use the file and large-scale correlational evidence agrees.
5. **CO-065 — Citable content carries provenance.** Content built to be cited uses original data, named sources, direct quotations, and statistics with their source stated on the page — the methods the peer-reviewed GEO study measured; keyword stuffing is not a GEO method.
6. **CO-066 — Citability never overrides real content.** Every statistic, quotation, or credential added for citability passes real-content first: it traces to fact-sheet.md or a producible source record, or it is cut. An invented figure is a blocker even if an engine cites it.
7. **CO-067 — Brand facts are identical everywhere.** Name, offer, prices, and locations are word-for-word consistent across the site and major third-party profiles (business listings, directories, review platforms); engines synthesize across sources, so an off-site contradiction is treated as a site contradiction.
8. **CO-068 — One canonical statement per fact.** Each brand fact an engine might quote is stated once, canonically, on an owned page, and other pages link to or reuse that statement rather than re-typing a variant.
9. **CO-069 — Citation measurement uses a fixed prompt panel.** Measurement runs a fixed, written set of prompts per engine on a set cadence, with engine, model/version where shown, date, and cited sources logged per run; the panel changes only by a recorded decision.
10. **CO-070 — A single answer is an anecdote.** No report, dashboard, or client update presents one screenshot or one run as a citation result; reports show the panel, the number of runs, and the variance across runs.
11. **CO-071 — No guaranteed outcomes.** No plan, proposal, or report promises AI citation, inclusion, or a visibility percentage; peer-reviewed effects are quoted only with their limits (study's models, method, and "up to" bound), never as an expected average.
12. **CO-072 — Structured data matches visible text.** Any structured data on a page targeted for citation describes only what the page visibly shows, with identical values; markup describing absent content is removed, not "optimized".

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-031 — AI citation guarantee.** Banned: promising or implying guaranteed citation, inclusion, or a fixed visibility lift in AI answers. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Instead: state the work and the measurement method, with each expected effect tagged by evidence level (CO-061, CO-071). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-032 — llms.txt reported as a visibility win.** Banned: listing llms.txt (or any special AI file/markup) in a results report as an AI-visibility achievement or requirement met. Defeats: DET-NONE — no DET parameter names this signal; governed by CO-064. Instead: record llms.txt as hygiene in the change log only; report citation results from the prompt panel (CO-064, CO-069). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-033 — Invented statistic added for citability.** Banned: adding a statistic, quotation, or study result to content to make it more citable without a producible source behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: cite a named source on the page or use the project's own measured data from fact-sheet.md — otherwise cut the figure (CO-066). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-034 — Vendor metric presented as a platform fact.** Banned: presenting a vendor's GEO score, correlation study, or lift figure as a search/AI platform's stated ranking or citation factor. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: label the study correlational, name its source, and treat it as a hypothesis the prompt panel can test (CO-061). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-CO-035 — Single-screenshot citation report.** Banned: reporting citation success or failure from one answer, one run, or one screenshot. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: report the fixed prompt panel over repeated dated runs, including runs where the brand is absent (CO-069, CO-070). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-031 — Evidence-tag audit.** Verifies: CO-061, CO-071. Check: manual checklist over the GEO plan/report — every tactic and claim carries one of the four evidence tags, and every peer-reviewed figure is quoted with its limits. Pass: 100% tagged, no guarantees anywhere in the document. Fail: return the plan for tagging before any work starts.
- **G-CO-032 — Citation-claim provenance scan.** Verifies: CO-065, CO-066. Check: automated assist plus manual verdict — extract every statistic and attributed quotation from pages in the GEO set (`grep -rEo '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?%' pages/ | sort -u`) and trace each to fact-sheet.md or a named on-page source. Pass: every figure traces; zero untraced figures. Fail: block shipment of the page.
- **G-CO-033 — Brand-fact consistency diff.** Verifies: CO-067, CO-068. Check: build the fact table (name, offer, prices, locations) from the site and each major third-party profile; diff every value against fact-sheet.md. Pass: zero conflicting values across all surfaces. Fail: correct the wrong surface before the measurement cycle starts.
- **G-CO-034 — Prompt-panel run log.** Verifies: CO-069, CO-070. Check: the citation tracker contains the fixed prompt set, one row per run with date, engine, and cited sources, and at least the scheduled number of runs for the period. Pass: log complete; reports cite panel aggregates only. Fail: mark the period's GEO results "insufficient data" — never substitute a single run.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Every tactic and claim in the plan carries an evidence-level tag (CO-061, G-CO-031).
- [ ] Documented fundamentals verified: indexed, snippet-eligible, crawlable at CDN/hosting level, textual content, internal links (CO-062).
- [ ] No file, markup, or vendor score is presented as a platform requirement or metric (CO-063).
- [ ] Every statistic and quotation in GEO-targeted pages traces to fact-sheet.md or a named source (CO-066, G-CO-032).
- [ ] Brand facts diffed identical across the site and major third-party profiles (CO-067, G-CO-033).
- [ ] Citation results come from the fixed prompt panel over repeated dated runs — no single-run claims (CO-069, CO-070, G-CO-034).
- [ ] No guarantee of citation, inclusion, or visibility percentage appears anywhere in the deliverable (CO-071).

# growth-experiments

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** web-analytics, real-content
- **Feeds into:** content-strategy, copywriting

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an A/B test or controlled experiment on a page, flow, price display, or message is being planned, launched, read, or reported — and whenever an experiment result is cited in a decision, brief, or report.
- **Do NOT use when:** the change is a defect fix or a legal/compliance requirement (ship it; do not test whether to fix a bug), the question is what the data says without an intervention (use web-analytics), or the variant copy itself is being written (use copywriting — this skill governs the test around it).

## Rules

1. **CO-261 — Registered before launch.** Every experiment exists in the experiment register before it receives traffic, with: a hypothesis tied to a named user problem, exactly one primary metric, guardrail metrics, the surface it runs on, and an owner. An unregistered test does not launch.
2. **CO-262 — Sample size and runtime computed in advance.** Before launch, the register records the pre-computed sample size per variant, the expected traffic split, and a fixed end date covering at least one full business cycle for the surface (a full week minimum on weekly-cycle traffic). "Run it until it looks significant" is not a runtime.
3. **CO-263 — No peeking decisions.** Results are read at the pre-registered horizon. The only exception is a sequential-testing method (e.g. an alpha-spending or always-valid p-value approach) named in the register before launch. A test stopped early because a variant was "winning" is void and is recorded as void.
4. **CO-264 — The primary metric decides.** The ship / kill / extend decision follows the primary metric alone. Secondary metrics may generate the next hypothesis; they never overturn, soften, or substitute for the primary result.
5. **CO-265 — One experiment per surface.** Two experiments never run on the same surface at the same time unless the register records an interaction-aware design (mutually exclusive buckets or a factorial design) before either launches.
6. **CO-266 — Random assignment, verified split.** Traffic is assigned randomly at the pre-registered split, and a sample ratio mismatch (SRM) check runs before any result is read. An SRM failure invalidates the experiment: the result is not interpreted, the assignment bug is fixed, and the test restarts.
7. **CO-267 — Effect size with a confidence interval.** Every reported result states the primary-metric effect size and its confidence interval, the sample sizes, and the runtime. A bare "significant" / "not significant" verdict, or a percentage lift with no interval, is not a reportable result.
8. **CO-268 — Variants pass the real-content gates.** Variant copy and claims pass the same gates as any shipped page before launch: no fabricated claim or statistic, no unsubstantiated superlative (DET-CON-026), no promise without a backing process (DET-CON-028). An experiment never tests whether a false claim converts better.
9. **CO-269 — Every conclusion is recorded, including losers.** At the horizon, the register entry is completed with the SRM result, the primary-metric effect and interval, and the decision (ship, kill, or inconclusive-extend with its reason). Losing and inconclusive experiments are recorded with the same completeness as winners; an experiment with no completed entry is treated as never having run.
10. **CO-270 — Guardrails can veto a win.** If a guardrail metric (e.g. revenue per visitor, unsubscribe rate, page performance, error rate) degrades beyond the bound set in the register, the variant does not ship even when the primary metric improves; the conflict is recorded in the entry.
11. **CO-271 — No mid-flight changes.** Variant content, traffic split, primary metric, and end date do not change after launch. A needed change closes the experiment as inconclusive and restarts it under a new register ID with the change recorded.
12. **CO-272 — Reports trace to the register.** Any number quoted from an experiment — in a report, brief, case study, or page — matches the register entry and its underlying results export exactly. Screenshots of a dashboard mid-flight and recollected figures are not sources.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-131 — The peek-and-stop win.** Banned: ending an experiment before its pre-registered horizon because an interim look showed a variant ahead, and reporting that lead as a result. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: run to the registered horizon (or use a sequential method named in advance, CO-263) and report the effect with its confidence interval. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-132 — The secondary-metric rescue.** Banned: declaring success on a secondary metric after the primary metric came back flat or negative. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: record the decision the primary metric dictates (CO-264); log the secondary observation as the hypothesis for a new registered experiment. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-133 — Testing a fabricated claim.** Banned: putting an invented statistic, testimonial, or unsubstantiated superlative into a variant to see if it lifts conversion. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Instead: variants use only fact-sheet-backed claims (CO-268); test the presentation of a true claim, never the invention of one. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-134 — The unrecorded experiment.** Banned: running, stopping, or citing an experiment that has no register entry, or quoting its outcome from memory or a dashboard screenshot. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: no entry, no experiment (CO-261); results are cited only from a completed register entry and its export (CO-272). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-135 — The unbacked-promise variant.** Banned: testing a variant whose offer, guarantee, or service promise has no backing policy or process behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: the promise ships in a variant only when the process that makes it true exists and is linked (CO-268). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-131 — SRM check (automated).** Verifies: CO-266. Check: in the results pipeline, run the chi-square test on observed vs expected assignment counts, e.g. `python3 -c "from scipy.stats import chisquare; print(chisquare([5231, 4769], f_exp=[5000, 5000]))"` with the experiment's real counts substituted. Pass: p-value > 0.001. Fail: the result is void — do not read the metrics; fix the assignment, record the failure, restart.
- **G-CO-132 — Pre-launch registration check.** Verifies: CO-261, CO-262, CO-265. Check: `grep -A 12 "EXP-<id>" experiments/register.md` and confirm the entry shows the hypothesis, one primary metric, guardrails, pre-computed sample size, fixed end date, surface, and owner — and that no other active entry names the same surface. Pass: all fields present, surface exclusive. Fail: block the launch until the entry is complete.
- **G-CO-133 — Variant real-content pass.** Verifies: CO-268. Check: extract every claim, figure, and promise from each variant and trace it to fact-sheet.md or a producible source record; assist with `grep -niE "best|#1|guarantee|risk-free|trusted by|% (faster|better|more)" variants/<id>/` and clear or cut each hit. Pass: every claim traced. Fail: the variant does not launch.
- **G-CO-134 — Horizon and decision audit.** Verifies: CO-263, CO-264, CO-269. Check: manual audit of the last concluded experiment — the decision date is on or after the registered end date, the recorded decision follows the primary metric, and the entry carries the SRM result, effect size, and confidence interval. Pass: all four hold. Fail: the conclusion is withdrawn, the entry corrected, and the result is not cited anywhere until it passes.
- **G-CO-135 — Register completeness sweep.** Verifies: CO-269, CO-272. Check: list every experiment marked concluded in the register; each has a completed entry (hypothesis, primary metric, SRM, effect, decision), including losers and inconclusive runs. Pass: zero concluded experiments with incomplete entries. Fail: complete the entries from the results exports before any new launch.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Register entry complete before launch: hypothesis, one primary metric, guardrails, owner (G-CO-132).
- [ ] Sample size computed and end date fixed, covering at least one full business cycle (CO-262).
- [ ] Surface is exclusive to this experiment, or an interaction-aware design is recorded (CO-265).
- [ ] Every variant claim traced to the fact sheet — no invented figures, superlatives, or unbacked promises (G-CO-133).
- [ ] SRM check passed before any metric was read (G-CO-131).
- [ ] Decision taken at the horizon, on the primary metric, with guardrails checked (CO-263, CO-264, CO-270).
- [ ] Register entry completed with effect size, confidence interval, SRM result, and decision — win, loss, or inconclusive (G-CO-135).

# internal-linking

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** technical-seo, sitemaps
- **Feeds into:** content-strategy, aeo, geo

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** designing a site's navigation, hubs, and breadcrumbs; publishing or retiring any page; reviewing a crawl; or diagnosing a page that gets no organic or referral traffic.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is which URLs exist in the sitemap file (sitemaps — the sitemap is a fallback, never the linking strategy), what a page says (copywriting, on-page-seo), or whether a URL should exist at all (content-strategy).

## Rules

1. **CO-201 — No orphan pages.** Every indexable page is linked from at least one non-sitemap page. An indexable page with zero inbound internal links is a defect, and every defect gets a named owner and a fix date.
2. **CO-202 — Shallow depth.** Every indexable page is reachable from the home page in at most 3 clicks by following links. Depth is measured on the crawl-derived link graph, never estimated.
3. **CO-203 — The brief names inbound links first.** Every new page's content brief names its planned inbound links (source page + anchor text) before the page is written. A page with no planned inbound links does not enter production.
4. **CO-204 — Anchor text describes the destination.** Anchor text names the destination page's topic, so it reads correctly out of context. "Click here", "here", and a bare "read more" are never the anchor for a content link.
5. **CO-205 — One anchor, one destination.** Identical anchor text never points to two different pages, and one destination is not linked under contradictory names. Collisions found in a crawl are renamed until each anchor maps to exactly one page.
6. **CO-206 — Link the canonical URL directly.** Internal links point at the canonical URL itself. No internal link may resolve through a redirect: if the target moved, the link is updated to the new URL in the same change.
7. **CO-207 — Critical pages earn in-content links.** Pricing, signup, and flagship content pages receive deliberate in-content links from relevant high-traffic pages. Nav or footer placement alone does not satisfy this rule.
8. **CO-208 — Retirement is one change.** When a page is retired or merged, its inbound internal links are updated or removed and its redirect is added in the same change — never in a later cleanup.
9. **CO-209 — The link graph is reviewed per release.** Every release produces a crawl-derived link graph (depth, in-degree, orphan list) and the review is recorded. A release with no graph review does not ship link or template changes.
10. **CO-210 — Hubs and breadcrumbs carry the structure.** Every section has a hub page that links its children, and every child page links back via breadcrumb or hub. No section is reachable only through site search or the sitemap.
11. **CO-211 — No broken internal links.** Every internal link resolves to a live page returning HTTP 200. A link to a 404, an error page, or an empty route is a defect with an owner, fixed like any other broken feature.
12. **CO-212 — Links are placed for readers.** A link exists because a reader at that point benefits from the destination. Link blocks, footer dumps, and pages built only to pass crawl equity to other pages are not a linking strategy.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-101 — Sitemap-only discovery.** Banned: shipping an indexable page whose only discovery path is the XML sitemap, with no inbound link from any real page. Defeats: DET-CON-025. Instead: add at least one in-content inbound link from a relevant page before publish (CO-201, CO-203). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-102 — Generic anchor text.** Banned: using "click here", "here", or "read more" as the anchor text for content links. Defeats: DET-CON-006. Instead: write the anchor as the destination's topic — "See pricing plans", "Read the API docs", "Read the Acme case study" (CO-204). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-103 — Anchor promises the destination doesn't keep.** Banned: anchor text naming a topic, offer, or document the destination page does not contain. Defeats: DET-CON-022. Instead: make the anchor describe what the destination actually delivers, or create the promised page and link that (CO-204). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-104 — Same anchor, different destinations.** Banned: one anchor string (e.g. "Our platform") linking to the product page in one place, the home page in another, and a landing page in a third. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: assign each anchor string exactly one destination site-wide and rename the variants (CO-205). Severity: WARN.
- **BAN-CO-105 — Template and staging links shipped live.** Banned: production navigation, footer, or body links still pointing at scaffold demo pages, a staging host, or placeholder routes from the site template. Defeats: DET-CON-002. Instead: repoint every shipped link at the real production page or remove it, and verify with the G-CO-102 scan before release. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-101 — Orphan and depth report.** Verifies: CO-201, CO-202, CO-210. Check: automated — crawl the production site, build the link graph, and list every indexable URL with in-degree 0 (sitemap excluded as a link source) plus every URL deeper than 3 clicks from home. Pass: zero orphans and zero pages deeper than 3 clicks. Fail: block the release; each orphan is assigned a named owner in progress.md.
- **G-CO-102 — Direct-target scan.** Verifies: CO-206, CO-211. Check: automated — request every internal href found by the crawl and record the status chain. Pass: 100% of internal links return HTTP 200 with no redirect hop. Fail: block shipment of the affected templates until links point at canonical URLs directly.
- **G-CO-103 — Anchor-text audit.** Verifies: CO-204, CO-205. Check: semi-automated — grep the rendered pages for the banned anchor strings ("click here", "here", "read more" as the complete anchor) and group all anchors by string to find one string mapping to multiple URLs; then manually read a sample of 20 in-content anchors against their destinations. Pass: zero banned anchors, zero multi-destination anchor strings, and every sampled anchor describes its destination. Fail: rework the failing anchors and re-run.
- **G-CO-104 — New-page inbound check.** Verifies: CO-203, CO-207. Check: manual — at publish, open each inbound link named in the page's brief and confirm it is live on the production page it was planned from, with the planned anchor text. Pass: every planned inbound link exists live at publish. Fail: do not announce or promote the page until the links are in place.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Crawl graph generated this release: zero orphan indexable pages (G-CO-101).
- [ ] Every indexable page is within 3 clicks of home (G-CO-101).
- [ ] Every internal link returns 200 directly — no redirect hops, no 404 targets (G-CO-102).
- [ ] No "click here" / "here" / bare "read more" anchors anywhere (G-CO-103).
- [ ] No anchor string points to more than one destination (G-CO-103).
- [ ] Each new page's brief named its inbound links, and they are live at publish (G-CO-104).
- [ ] Pricing, signup, and flagship pages have in-content links from relevant high-traffic pages (CO-207).
- [ ] Any retired page had its inbound links updated and its redirect added in the same change (CO-208).

<!-- generated from skills/seo-content/lifecycle-email/SKILL.md (bundle form, rung 2) -->

# lifecycle-email

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** fact-sheet, real-content
- **Feeds into:** growth-experiments, web-analytics

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** designing, editing, or auditing a behavior-triggered message program — onboarding, activation, engagement, retention, or win-back journeys across email, push, or in-app — including its authentication, consent, suppression, and measurement setup.
- **Do NOT use when:** the message is transactional (receipts, password resets, security alerts — that is D11's transactional-email skill, on its own stream), when the message is an incident or status communication (D18), or when the task is a one-off page or post (copywriting).

## Rules

1. **CO-141 — Authentication before volume.** SPF, DKIM, and an aligned DMARC record (minimum p=none) exist and verify on every sending domain before any program sends from it; no journey launches on an unauthenticated domain.
2. **CO-142 — Consent is a send-time check.** Every send verifies the profile's current opt-in status for that message type at send time; a signup-time consent memory never substitutes for the check, and an opt-out recorded anywhere suppresses everywhere for that type.
3. **CO-143 — Streams are never mixed.** Marketing journeys send only from the marketing stream and subdomain; transactional mail never carries marketing content to borrow transactional consent or deliverability, and marketing mail never rides the transactional stream.
4. **CO-144 — Every journey is fully specified.** Each journey names its lifecycle stage, entry event, exit events (stored on the user profile), conversion goal, owner, and one primary metric before it is built; an unspecified journey is not launched.
5. **CO-145 — Every journey carries a control group.** A fixed holdout of eligible users receives no journey messages, so the journey's effect on its primary metric is measured against the control, never assumed from opens or clicks alone.
6. **CO-146 — Merge fields ship with tested fallbacks.** Every personalization field has a fallback value or a fallback rendering (e.g. a greeting that works with no first name), and the fallback path is exercised in testing, not just written.
7. **CO-147 — Seed-send after every edit.** After any journey or template edit, the full sequence is sent to seed accounts on every channel it uses, and the rendered messages are read before the edit goes live.
8. **CO-148 — Suppression is part of the journey definition.** Each journey's exit and exclusion logic is event-based: win-back excludes anyone who purchased or was active inside the stage's window, and re-entry is blocked while a user is inside another conflicting journey.
9. **CO-149 — Frequency caps stop stage collisions.** A per-user cap across all journeys (per day and per week) is enforced by the sending platform, so onboarding, engagement, and win-back messages can never stack on the same user in the same window.
10. **CO-150 — Subject lines and headers are honest.** No deceptive subject lines, no fake "Re:" or "Fwd:" prefixes, no sender names implying a person or relationship that does not exist; the subject states what the message actually contains (CAN-SPAM).
11. **CO-151 — Lists are earned and sunset.** Recipients come only from the product's own opt-in capture — never purchased, rented, or scraped lists — and profiles with no engagement inside the documented sunset window are suppressed from regular sends and eventually removed.
12. **CO-152 — Unsubscribe is one click and honored fast.** Marketing mail carries one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe-Post) where the bulk-sender regime applies, every opt-out is honored within 48 hours (inside the CAN-SPAM 10-business-day legal floor), and the sending domain's spam rate is kept under 0.3%.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-071 — Unrendered merge field in production.** Banned: a live message containing raw template tokens or stringified empty values. Defeats: DET-CON-003. Instead: give every field a tested fallback and pass the seed-send rendering test before the edit goes live (CO-146, CO-147). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-072 — Fabricated familiarity.** Banned: personalization that asserts a history, tenure, or preference the profile does not record. Defeats: DET-CON-014. Instead: render tenure and history claims only from profile fields, and omit the claim when the field is absent (CO-146). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-073 — Invented social proof in email copy.** Banned: statistics, ratings, or customer counts in a message with no source record behind them. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: use only figures with a fact-sheet.md entry that agree everywhere they appear, or cut the claim (real-content). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-074 — Deceptive subject line.** Banned: a subject that promises an outcome, reply, or document that does not exist. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: write a subject that states the message's real content and offer (CO-150). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-075 — Behavior-blind win-back.** Banned: a generic "we miss you" journey whose audience is defined by signup date alone, with no event-based suppression. Defeats: DET-CON-006. Instead: define entry and suppression by events — exclude recent purchasers and active users inside the stage window (CO-148). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CO-071 — DNS authentication check.** Verifies: CO-141. Check: automated in CI for every sending domain — `dig +short TXT example.com` shows an SPF record, `dig +short TXT selector._domainkey.example.com` returns the DKIM key, `dig +short TXT _dmarc.example.com` returns a DMARC record, and the DMARC domain aligns with the From domain. Pass: all three records present and aligned. Fail: block sending from that domain.
- **G-CO-072 — Seed-send rendering test.** Verifies: CO-146, CO-147. Check: automated — after any journey edit, send the full sequence to seed accounts, capture the rendered messages, and scan them for unrendered tokens: `grep -E '\{\{|}}|undefined|null|NaN' rendered/` returns nothing. Pass: zero token hits on every channel. Fail: block the edit from going live.
- **G-CO-073 — Journey audit.** Verifies: CO-144, CO-145, CO-148, CO-149. Check: manual checklist per journey — stage, entry event, exit events, conversion goal, owner, primary metric, control group, event-based suppression, and the cross-journey frequency cap are all present in the journey definition. Pass: every field present. Fail: journey stays in draft.
- **G-CO-074 — Consent and deliverability check.** Verifies: CO-142, CO-151, CO-152. Check: automated pre-send audience assertion — every profile in the send list has a current opt-in record for the message type and is not on the suppression or sunset list — plus a weekly spam-rate review per sending domain. Pass: 100% of recipients verified opted-in, spam rate under 0.3%. Fail: halt the send and clean the audience.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] SPF, DKIM, and aligned DMARC verify on every sending domain (CO-141, G-CO-071).
- [ ] Every journey names stage, entry/exit events, goal, owner, and primary metric (CO-144).
- [ ] Every journey has a control group and event-based suppression (CO-145, CO-148).
- [ ] Send-time opt-in check and cross-journey frequency cap are enforced (CO-142, CO-149).
- [ ] Seed-send rendering test passes with zero unrendered tokens (G-CO-072).
- [ ] One-click unsubscribe present and opt-outs honored within 48 hours (CO-152).
- [ ] No purchased or scraped addresses anywhere in the audience (CO-151).
- [ ] Every statistic or social-proof claim in copy has a fact-sheet entry (BAN-CO-073).

<!-- generated from skills/seo-content/on-page-seo/SKILL.md (bundle form, rung 2) -->

# on-page-seo

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** technical-seo, fact-sheet
- **Feeds into:** aeo, geo, structured-data, internal-linking

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** an indexable page is created, rewritten, or audited — assigning its search intent, writing its title, H1, heading outline, body, and meta description, or resolving two pages that compete for the same query.
- **Do NOT use when:** the problem is crawlability, indexation, canonicals, or rendering (use technical-seo), when the deliverable is structured data markup (use structured-data), or when the page is non-indexable app UI that no searcher should land on.

## Rules

1. **CO-021 — One page, one primary intent.** Every indexable page is mapped in the intent map to exactly one primary search intent drawn from real query data (Search Console or documented keyword research); a page with no mapped intent is not published as indexable.
2. **CO-022 — Metadata is written last.** The title and meta description are written from the finished page content, never from the brief or template, so both describe what the visitor actually gets.
3. **CO-023 — Unique title and description per page.** No two indexable pages share a title or a meta description, and neither is ever a template default or placeholder string.
4. **CO-024 — Titles state topic and offer plainly.** A title names the page's topic and its concrete offer in natural language a searcher would type; it contains no repeated keyword variants and no claim the page does not support.
5. **CO-025 — One H1, real heading outline.** Each page has exactly one H1 matching its primary intent, and H2/H3 headings form a true outline of the page's argument in reading order — no heading exists only to hold a keyword.
6. **CO-026 — Body satisfies the intent first.** The page's opening section answers the primary query directly with page-specific facts; supporting sections expand it. Generic filler that could sit on any competitor's page is cut.
7. **CO-027 — Descriptions promise only what the page delivers.** Every offer, price, feature, or outcome named in the meta description appears on the page itself, worded consistently with fact-sheet.md.
8. **CO-028 — Intent collisions are resolved in writing.** When a new page targets an intent an existing page owns, the intent map records the resolution before publication: merge, redirect, or a written differentiation (page-specific facts, audience, or format).
9. **CO-029 — Claims on the page are sourced or removed.** Any statistic, ranking, or superlative in title, headings, or body carries a citation on the page or in fact-sheet.md; unmeasurable superlatives ("best", "leading") are deleted, not softened.
10. **CO-030 — Intent map is re-checked quarterly.** The top indexable pages are sampled against Search Console query data each quarter; a page whose real queries no longer match its mapped intent is reassigned, merged, or rewritten.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-011 — Keyword-stuffed title.** Banned: a title that repeats keyword variants or lists services instead of stating the topic plainly. Defeats: DET-CON-022. Instead: state the topic and offer once, in natural language: `<title>Running Shoes for Flat Feet — Fit Guide & Picks</title>`. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-012 — Duplicate or default metadata.** Banned: the same title or meta description on multiple pages, or template defaults shipped to production. Defeats: DET-CON-022. Instead: write a unique title and description per page from its finished content (CO-022, CO-023). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-013 — Meta description advertising an absent offer.** Banned: a description that promises a discount, feature, or outcome the page does not contain. Defeats: DET-CON-022. Instead: describe only what the page delivers, consistent with fact-sheet.md (CO-027). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-014 — Scaled near-duplicate intent pages.** Banned: publishing many pages that target the same intent with swapped nouns (city, product, audience) and no page-specific substance. Defeats: DET-CON-025. Instead: merge into one strong page, or differentiate each with real page-specific facts, audience, or format recorded in the intent map (CO-028). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-015 — Unsubstantiated superlative in title or body.** Banned: "the best", "#1", "leading" or similar claims with no cited substantiation. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Instead: state the verifiable fact ("Used by 4,000 teams", with the figure in fact-sheet.md) or drop the claim (CO-029). Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CO-011 — Metadata lint.** Verifies: CO-023, CO-024. Check: automated CI lint over the route inventory — extract every indexable page's `<title>` and meta description and fail on duplicates, missing values, or placeholder strings: `grep -rhoP '(?<=<title>).*?(?=</title>)' dist/ | sort | uniq -d` returns nothing, and the same for descriptions. Pass: zero duplicates, zero missing, zero defaults. Fail: block shipment.
- **G-CO-012 — Intent map coverage.** Verifies: CO-021, CO-028. Check: diff the indexable route inventory against the intent map; every route has exactly one primary intent and every collision has a recorded resolution. Pass: 100% coverage, no unresolved collisions. Fail: block shipment of the unmapped page.
- **G-CO-013 — Description-to-page promise check.** Verifies: CO-022, CO-027. Check: manual sample — for each new or changed page, list every offer named in the meta description and point to the page section that delivers it. Pass: every promise located on the page and consistent with fact-sheet.md. Fail: rewrite the description before release.
- **G-CO-014 — Heading outline check.** Verifies: CO-025. Check: automated — parse each indexable page and assert exactly one H1 and no skipped heading levels: a DOM query for `h1` returns count 1 per page. Pass: all pages conform. Fail: fix the outline and re-run.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Every indexable page is in the intent map with exactly one primary intent (CO-021).
- [ ] Title and meta description were written or re-checked against the finished page (CO-022).
- [ ] Metadata lint passes: no duplicate, missing, or default titles/descriptions (G-CO-011).
- [ ] Exactly one H1 per page and headings form a real outline (CO-025, G-CO-014).
- [ ] Every offer in each description is delivered on its page and matches fact-sheet.md (CO-027).
- [ ] No unsubstantiated superlatives or unsourced statistics in titles, headings, or body (CO-029).
- [ ] Every intent collision has a written merge, redirect, or differentiation (CO-028).

# real-content

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** fact-sheet (D1)
- **Feeds into:** copywriting, structured-data, content-strategy, growth-experiments

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** Any page, post, email, metadata set, or JSON-LD block is about to publish and contains a factual element — a testimonial, review, statistic, credential, person, price, promise, or byline. This skill is the pre-publish enforcement pass for the Real Content Rule (QB-10).
- **Do NOT use when:** Drafting copy from scratch (use copywriting, then run this pass on the result), deciding whether a claim is legal in a specific jurisdiction (route to D14 legal-privacy — this skill blocks, it does not give legal advice), or checking code-level fake functionality (use D8 placeholder-scan and the DET-FAKE parameters).

## Rules

1. **CO-121 — Classify before you publish.** Before publication, list every factual element in the piece and classify it: testimonial, review, statistic, credential, person, price, promise, or authorship. Each element is matched to its evidence — a source record the business can produce, a fact-sheet.md entry, or the live data the page renders from. An element with no match does not ship.
2. **CO-122 — The blocker list is absolute.** A fabricated testimonial (DET-CON-010), review set (DET-CON-013), third-party statistic (DET-CON-011), credential or press claim (DET-CON-012), or person (DET-CON-019) fails the entire content pass. There is no "mostly real" grade and no averaging against the elements that check out.
3. **CO-123 — First-party counters are not exempt.** A self-attested usage counter ("84 million accounts") needs a fact-sheet.md entry recording its source system and as-of date, and the same figure must appear everywhere it is used (DET-CON-011 check (b), DET-CON-015). A counter contradicted by another page is a fail; a consistent counter with no fact-sheet entry is a gap to close before publish, not a pass.
4. **CO-124 — Prices come from one source.** Every price, plan name, and billing term renders from the single pricing data source and is verified against a test checkout total before publish. A marketing page may never carry a price the checkout contradicts (DET-CON-016). Promotions carry visible dates and terms.
5. **CO-125 — No backing artifact, no promise.** Every operational promise — support hours, response times, guarantees, refund and cancellation terms — links to the policy page or documented process that makes it true (DET-CON-028). If the backing artifact does not exist, the promise is removed, not reworded.
6. **CO-126 — Bylines name real people or an honest house byline.** An individual byline requires an author page plus one independent trace (staff page, professional profile). Genuinely collective content may use an accountable team byline ("The Support Team"). An invented individual is never acceptable (DET-CON-020).
7. **CO-127 — Cut, don't soften.** An element with no evidence is deleted. It is never rescued with hedges ("up to", "as much as", "customers love us"), moved to a less prominent slot, or kept "until we get the real one." Placeholder social proof is fabrication with a deadline.
8. **CO-128 — Metadata and structured data pass the same gate.** Titles, meta descriptions, OG tags, and JSON-LD fields are factual elements under CO-121. Every JSON-LD rating, price, date, and author has a visible counterpart with an identical value, or a fact-sheet entry (DET-CON-024). Review markup exists only where real, visible reviews exist.
9. **CO-129 — A named human verifies the facts.** AI may draft and assemble evidence, but a named person checks each classified element against its source and records their name and the date in progress.md before publish. "The model wrote it" is not a verification step.
10. **CO-130 — Dated claims have owners and expiry.** Every date-bearing claim (sale end, event date, "new for <year>") carries an owner and a review-by date. Expired promotions and past events presented as current are removed or reframed as archive at the review date (DET-CON-018).
11. **CO-131 — Team imagery is real or absent.** Portraits captioned with employee names and roles are photographs of those people. Where no real photo exists, the page runs without a portrait — never a stock image or generated face in its place (DET-CON-019).
12. **CO-132 — Block and route legal questions; never improvise them.** Superlatives, guarantees, review displays, and testimonial use can be advertising-law questions. This skill blocks the element and routes the question to D14; it never clears a claim by arguing the law itself.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-061 — Invented testimonial.** Banned: a quoted endorsement from a person whose quote the business cannot produce as a source record. Defeats: DET-CON-010. Instead: publish only quotes held as source records (email, platform review, signed quote) with permission, or ship the section with no testimonial. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-062 — Unsourced third-party statistic.** Banned: a rating, market, benchmark, or comparison figure with no provenance anywhere on the domain or on file. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: cite the dataset or platform the figure came from, or delete the figure and describe the product plainly. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-063 — Substitute people.** Banned: a stock photograph or generated portrait captioned as a named employee, founder, or customer. Defeats: DET-CON-019. Instead: use a real photograph of the named person, or publish the name and role with no portrait. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-064 — Unbacked promise.** Banned: a present-tense operational promise with no policy or process behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: link the promise to the policy or documented process that honors it, or remove the promise and state the actual terms. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-065 — Seed people presented as real users.** Banned: demo, seed, or sample accounts, reviews, or activity shipped in production copy as real customers or demand. Defeats: DET-FAKE-014. Instead: exclude seed data from production surfaces entirely; social proof comes only from real, attributable users. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-061 — Claim-trace audit.** Verifies: CO-121, CO-123, CO-124. Check: run `python3 scripts/claim-trace.py --pages dist/ --fact-sheet fact-sheet.md` — the script extracts checkable facts (numbers, prices, dates, names) from the rendered pages and diffs them against fact-sheet.md, exiting non-zero on any unmatched or contradicted fact. Pass: exit code 0; every extracted fact traces to a fact-sheet entry. Fail: block publication; fix the copy or the stale fact-sheet side and record which was corrected.
- **G-CO-062 — DET-CON pre-publish scan.** Verifies: CO-122, CO-127, CO-128, CO-130. Check: run the DET-CON-001…028 checks over the rendered pages, metadata, and JSON-LD; the automatable subset runs as `python3 scripts/det-con-scan.py --pages dist/` (placeholder strings, template tokens, date extraction, JSON-LD-vs-page field diff), and the remaining parameters (010–013, 019, 020, 028) are worked as a manual checklist against the evidence register. Pass: zero blocker hits and zero unaddressed major hits. Fail: block publication — one fabricated element fails the whole pass.
- **G-CO-063 — Evidence register completeness.** Verifies: CO-121, CO-122, CO-126. Check: for every testimonial, review, statistic, credential, and byline in the piece, the evidence register holds a source-record reference (file path, platform URL, or fact-sheet line). Pass: counts match and both spot-checks support their claims. Fail: block publication; the unsupported element is cut under CO-127.
- **G-CO-064 — Named human verification.** Verifies: CO-129. Check: progress.md contains the verifier's name, the date, and the list of pages passed, entered before the publish timestamp. **Human-required:** the verifier is by definition a named human; no automated or agent-produced substitute satisfies this gate, and autonomous publication is blocked until the human entry exists. Pass: entry present and complete. Fail: block publication until a named human has done the check — an automated pass alone never satisfies this gate.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Every factual element is classified and matched to evidence (CO-121).
- [ ] Zero blocker-list fabrications: testimonials, reviews, statistics, credentials, people (CO-122).
- [ ] Every first-party counter has a fact-sheet entry and agrees site-wide (CO-123).
- [ ] Every price matches the pricing source and a test checkout total (CO-124).
- [ ] Every operational promise links to its backing policy or process (CO-125).
- [ ] Every byline is a real, traceable person or an honest house byline (CO-126).
- [ ] Claim-trace audit (G-CO-061) and DET-CON scan (G-CO-062) both pass.
- [ ] A named human has verified the facts and signed progress.md (CO-129, G-CO-064).
