# sitemaps

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** technical-seo
- **Feeds into:** internal-linking, web-analytics

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a site launches, migrates, restructures, or changes its route or content inventory, and whenever sitemap correctness, freshness, or Search Console sitemap errors are in question. This skill owns the sitemap as a generated claim about which URLs exist and are indexable.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is whether a page should be indexable or canonical at all (technical-seo sets that contract; this skill generates against it), or how pages get discovered by users (internal-linking — the sitemap is a crawler fallback, never a linking strategy).

## Rules

1. **CO-181 — Generated, never hand-maintained.** The sitemap is a build artifact generated from the actual route and content inventory at publish time. No sitemap file is ever edited by hand; a needed change is made in the inventory or the generator, never in the output.
2. **CO-182 — Canonical entries only.** Every listed URL returns HTTP 200, is indexable (no `noindex`, no robots block), and is its own canonical. An entry is a claim that the URL is live and canonical — if any leg fails, the URL does not belong in the file.
3. **CO-183 — No dead or redirected entries.** Redirects (3xx), errors (4xx/5xx), non-canonical variants, and parameter, filter, sort, or session URLs are never listed. The sitemap names destinations, not paths to them.
4. **CO-184 — One host, one scheme, absolute URLs.** Every entry is an absolute URL on the site's single canonical host and scheme (per technical-seo CO-009). No relative URLs, no mixed www/non-www, no HTTP entries on an HTTPS site.
5. **CO-185 — Truthful lastmod.** `lastmod` is the date the page's content last changed significantly, taken from the content record — never the build or deploy timestamp. When the change date is not known, omit `lastmod` rather than invent one; engines discount sitemaps whose dates cry wolf.
6. **CO-186 — Event-driven regeneration.** The sitemap regenerates in the same build or publish event that changes the inventory: publish, unpublish, route change, redirect change. A sitemap older than the newest content change is stale by definition and is a defect, not a backlog item.
7. **CO-187 — Protocol limits.** Each sitemap file holds at most 50,000 URLs and 50 MB uncompressed, per the sitemaps protocol. Beyond either limit, split into multiple files under a sitemap index. The limit is measured on the uncompressed file, even when the served file is gzipped.
8. **CO-188 — Shard by section.** Large sites shard sitemaps by content type or section (posts, products, docs) under one sitemap index, so a broken or stale section is visible in Search Console reporting instead of diluted across one giant file.
9. **CO-189 — Count reconciliation.** After every generation, the sitemap URL count is reconciled against the route/content inventory count. Every difference has a named reason (draft, noindex by design, redirect) recorded with the build; an unexplained difference fails the release.
10. **CO-190 — Discovery wiring.** The sitemap is referenced by a `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt and submitted in Search Console. After a domain change, restructure, or index rebuild, the submission is re-verified — the file existing on the server is not evidence any engine knows about it.
11. **CO-191 — Production purity.** A staging sitemap never deploys to production, and a production sitemap never lists staging hosts or staging URLs. The sitemap host check is part of technical-seo's staging-vs-production promotion diff.
12. **CO-192 — No invented priority or changefreq.** `priority` and `changefreq` are omitted, or set truthfully per section from the actual update pattern. Values that misstate the pages (1.0 and "always" site-wide) are fabricated metadata and are never emitted to look thorough.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-091 — Dead and excluded URLs listed.** Banned: a sitemap containing URLs that return 404/410, redirect, carry `noindex`, or canonicalize to a different URL. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: generate from the live inventory and filter on 200 + indexable + self-canonical before writing any entry (CO-182, CO-183). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-092 — Deploy-date lastmod.** Banned: stamping every entry's `lastmod` with the build or deploy date, so unchanged pages claim to have changed on every release. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: take `lastmod` from each content record's real change date, and omit it where that date is unknown (CO-185). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-093 — The hand-maintained sitemap.** Banned: a static `sitemap.xml` written or edited by hand — typically generated once at launch and shipped untouched ever after while the site changes around it. Defeats: DET-CON-002. Instead: the sitemap is generated from the route/content inventory on every publish event; hands never touch the output (CO-181, CO-186). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-094 — Variant URLs listed as pages.** Banned: listing parameter, filter, sort, session, or print variants as separate sitemap entries to inflate the URL count. Defeats: DET-CON-025. Instead: list only the canonical URL of each substantively distinct page (CO-183); variants canonicalize or carry `noindex` under technical-seo. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-095 — Staging URLs in the production sitemap.** Banned: a production sitemap listing staging hosts, preview URLs, or internal hostnames. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: generate against the production inventory on the canonical host only, and run the host check in the promotion diff (CO-184, CO-191). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-091 — Sitemap audit script.** Verifies: CO-182, CO-183, CO-184. Check: automated — `python3 scripts/sitemap_audit.py --sitemap https://example.com/sitemap.xml` fetches the sitemap (following the index to every shard), requests every listed URL (or a statistically sound random sample above 10,000 URLs), and asserts per URL: HTTP 200, no redirect, canonical tag equal to the listed URL, no `noindex` in meta robots or X-Robots-Tag, host and scheme equal to the canonical host. Pass: zero assertion failures. Fail: block the release; fix the inventory or generator, never the output file.
- **G-CO-092 — Count reconciliation.** Verifies: CO-181, CO-189. Check: automated — the build compares the generated sitemap's URL count against the route/content inventory count and writes both numbers plus a reason for every excluded inventory item (draft, noindex, redirect) to the build log. Pass: counts reconcile with every difference explained. Fail: block the release until the difference is explained.
- **G-CO-093 — Regeneration-on-change test.** Verifies: CO-181, CO-186. Check: automated — in the staging build, publish one test page and unpublish another, rebuild, and diff the sitemap: the published URL must appear and the unpublished URL must disappear, with no manual step. Pass: both changes reflected by the build alone. Fail: the generator is not wired to the inventory; fix before launch.
- **G-CO-094 — lastmod spot-check.** Verifies: CO-185. Check: automated assist — sample 25 entries carrying `lastmod` and compare each against the content record's actual last-change timestamp (CMS field or version-control history for that page's source). Pass: every sampled `lastmod` matches the record, or the entry omits `lastmod`. Fail: remove or correct the dates at the generator and re-run.
- **G-CO-095 — Discovery wiring check.** Verifies: CO-190, CO-191. Check: automated — fetch robots.txt and assert it contains a `Sitemap:` line naming the production sitemap index on the canonical host; fetch that URL and assert HTTP 200 and zero listed URLs on any non-production host. Pass: both assertions hold and the Search Console submission is confirmed in the project log. Fail: fix robots.txt or the generator's host configuration and re-check. Before a production environment is provisioned, this gate's disposition is a recorded provisioning waiver per the §6.3 protocol; it unblocks when the production site is deployed on its canonical host and Search Console access exists.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Sitemap generated from the route/content inventory in this build — no hand edits (CO-181).
- [ ] Audit script passes: every listed URL returns 200, self-canonical, indexable (G-CO-091).
- [ ] Sitemap count reconciles with the inventory count; every difference explained (G-CO-092).
- [ ] Publish/unpublish test changes the sitemap with no manual step (G-CO-093).
- [ ] Sampled `lastmod` values match real content change dates (G-CO-094).
- [ ] No staging host or non-canonical URL anywhere in the file (G-CO-095).
- [ ] Each file within 50,000 URLs / 50 MB uncompressed; index current (CO-187, CO-188).
- [ ] robots.txt names the sitemap and Search Console submission is confirmed (CO-190).

# social-open-graph

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** on-page-seo, technical-seo
- **Feeds into:** web-analytics

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a site launches, a page template is built or changed, branding changes, or a shared link previews the wrong title, description, or image. This skill owns the Open Graph and Twitter Card tags every public page emits.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is what the page itself says (copywriting, on-page-seo), what its JSON-LD declares (structured-data), or whether the page is indexable (technical-seo). Never use it to promise share traffic: platforms render the tags; they do not guarantee distribution.

## Rules

1. **CO-221 — The four required properties, on every public page.** Every public page emits `og:title`, `og:type`, `og:image`, and `og:url`, plus `og:description` and `og:site_name`. A page missing any required property is a defect, not a style choice.
2. **CO-222 — og:url is the page's canonical URL.** og:url equals the canonical URL technical-seo assigns the page. A site-wide homepage og:url on interior pages is a defect (DET-CON-023).
3. **CO-223 — og:title and og:description are per-page.** Both are generated from the page's own title and topic and match what the link actually opens. Identical og:title or og:description across pages with different destinations is a defect.
4. **CO-224 — og:image is absolute and page-appropriate.** og:image is an absolute URL (never a relative path a crawler cannot resolve) pointing to an image that represents this page, at full share size — the protocol's recommended 1200×630. The homepage logo is never the og:image for every page.
5. **CO-225 — The image fallback is a compromise, not the design.** Only og:image may fall back to a site-wide default share image, and that fallback is recorded as a known compromise. og:title, og:description, and og:url never fall back to site-wide values.
6. **CO-226 — og:site_name is this site's own name.** og:site_name carries the site's current name from the fact sheet, on every page. A scaffold's or another site's name in og:site_name is a defect.
7. **CO-227 — og:type matches the content, with its properties.** Pages use the og:type that fits (website for general pages, article for posts, product for product pages), and type-specific properties are emitted where they apply — article:published_time and article:author on posts.
8. **CO-228 — Twitter Card tags mirror the OG values.** twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description, and twitter:image are emitted and carry the same per-page values as their OG counterparts; twitter:card is summary_large_image wherever og:image meets the large-image size. Two metadata systems describing one page never disagree.
9. **CO-229 — Tags are generated in the page template.** OG and Twitter tags are produced by the page template from the page's own data — the same source that renders the visible title and description. Hand-edited per-page tag blocks and tags pasted from a scaffold or another site are defects.
10. **CO-230 — Share images are real assets.** Every og:image URL returns HTTP 200 and serves the image the tags claim. A purpose-built share image is produced for each page type; a stretched logo, a placeholder graphic, or a stock photo presented as the product is a defect.
11. **CO-231 — No private or gated page gets public card promises.** Pages behind authentication, staging hosts, and noindex pages do not emit OG tags describing them as public content, and production tags never point at staging URLs or staging images.
12. **CO-232 — Debuggers re-run after template or branding changes.** Social platforms cache previews aggressively, so after any template, branding, or share-image change, the home, article, and product templates are re-run through the platform debuggers to force fresh scrapes. A fix that is never re-scraped is not live.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-111 — Site-wide homepage og:url.** Banned: emitting the homepage URL as og:url on every page. Defeats: DET-CON-023. Instead: og:url is each page's own canonical URL, generated by the template (CO-222). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-112 — One og:title and og:description for the whole site.** Banned: a single global title/description pair in the social tags regardless of destination. Defeats: DET-CON-023. Instead: og:title and og:description are generated per page from that page's title and topic (CO-223). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-113 — Homepage logo as every page's og:image.** Banned: pointing og:image at the site logo or one generic brand graphic for all pages. Defeats: DET-CON-023. Instead: each page type gets a purpose-built share image representing its content; only a recorded fallback may reuse the default image (CO-224, CO-225). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-114 — Another site's identity in the tags.** Banned: og:site_name, og:title suffixes, or image URLs copied from a scaffold, theme demo, or another site and never replaced. Defeats: DET-CON-023. Instead: site_name and branding come from this site's fact sheet, and all tag assets are served from this site's own domain (CO-226, CO-229). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-115 — Relative or broken og:image.** Banned: og:image as a relative path, a staging URL, or a URL that does not return the claimed image. Defeats: DET-CON-023. Instead: og:image is an absolute production URL verified to return HTTP 200 with the intended image (CO-224, CO-230). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-111 — Site-wide tag dump diff.** Verifies: CO-221, CO-222, CO-223, CO-226. Check: automated — crawl every public URL, extract all OG and Twitter tags, and diff: og:url must equal the page's canonical URL, og:title/og:description must match the page's own title/topic with no cross-page duplicates across different destinations, og:site_name must equal the current brand name, and all four required properties must be present. Pass: zero mismatches. Fail: block shipment of the affected templates.
- **G-CO-112 — og:image resolution and size check.** Verifies: CO-224, CO-225, CO-230. Check: automated — request every distinct og:image URL; assert absolute URL, HTTP 200, image content type, and dimensions of 1200×630; flag any image reused across pages outside the recorded fallback list. Pass: every og:image resolves at full share size and reuse matches the fallback record, and every page without one carries the recorded no-image disposition. Fail: fix the asset or the template and re-run.
- **G-CO-113 — Platform debugger pass.** Verifies: CO-227, CO-228, CO-232. Check: manual — run the production home, article, and product URLs through the Meta Sharing Debugger and the X/Twitter card validator; confirm the rendered preview shows the page's own title, description, and image, and re-scrape after any template or branding change. Pass: all three templates preview correctly with current branding. Fail: correct the tags and force a re-scrape before launch sign-off.
- **G-CO-114 — Template generation audit.** Verifies: CO-229, CO-231. Check: automated grep plus manual review — search templates and rendered output for hardcoded og: tags, foreign domains, and staging hosts; confirm tags are emitted from page data and that gated/noindex pages carry no public card tags. Pass: no hardcoded or foreign tag values found; tags trace to the page template. Fail: move generation into the template and re-run G-CO-111.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Every public page emits og:title, og:type, og:image, og:url, og:description, and og:site_name (CO-221).
- [ ] Tag dump diff is clean: og:url equals canonical, no cross-page title/description duplicates (G-CO-111).
- [ ] Every og:image is absolute, returns 200, and is 1200×630 (G-CO-112).
- [ ] og:site_name matches the current brand name from the fact sheet (CO-226).
- [ ] Twitter Card tags mirror the OG values (CO-228).
- [ ] Home, article, and product templates pass the platform debuggers with current branding (G-CO-113).
- [ ] No hardcoded, foreign-domain, or staging values in any tag (G-CO-114).

# structured-data

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** real-content (whether reviews, ratings, and claims may exist at all), fact-sheet (D1, for page-external facts)
- **Feeds into:** technical-seo, aeo, web-analytics

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a page type gains, changes, or loses JSON-LD markup; a template or data model feeding markup changes; or Search Console reports a rich-result error. This skill owns the markup contract; D3 frontend implements the templates against it.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is whether the underlying content may be published (real-content decides), what the page says (copywriting), or whether the page is crawlable (technical-seo). Never use markup to make a claim the page itself does not make.

## Rules

1. **CO-161 — Generated, never hand-written.** Every JSON-LD block is emitted by a template from the same data store that renders the visible page. No per-page hand-edited or copy-pasted blocks exist; if a value is wrong, the fix lands in the data or the template, never in one page's markup.
2. **CO-162 — Markup says only what the page shows.** Every rating, price, date, author, and availability value in JSON-LD has a visible counterpart on the same page with an identical value. A field with no visible counterpart is removed, not "completed" (DET-CON-024).
3. **CO-163 — One template per page type, kept small.** A schema type is added only when pages of that type genuinely contain the content the type describes. Marking up content the page type does not have — a recipe schema on a product page — is a defect, not ambition.
4. **CO-164 — Required properties complete.** Each template carries every property Google requires for the rich result that page type is eligible for, plus recommended properties wherever the underlying data exists. Eligibility is checked against Google's structured-data documentation per type, not assumed.
5. **CO-165 — No placeholder values, ever.** Generator defaults — "Product Name", price `0.00`, `example.com` URLs, sample organization names — are build failures. A template that cannot populate a required property from real data does not ship.
6. **CO-166 — Review markup follows real reviews.** `Review` and `aggregateRating` markup exists only on pages where real reviews are visibly rendered and have passed real-content. The markup question is never asked before the real-content question is answered.
7. **CO-167 — Prices match everywhere.** `Offer.price` and `priceValidUntil` in markup are identical to the price rendered on the page and the price charged at checkout, drawn from the same price source (DET-CON-016). A sale that ended removes the offer markup in the same change.
8. **CO-168 — JSON-LD, syntactically valid.** JSON-LD is the only format. Every block parses as valid JSON — one trailing comma invalidates the whole block — and validation runs in the build, not by eyeball.
9. **CO-169 — Dates and authors match.** `datePublished`, `dateModified`, and `author` in markup are identical to the visible byline and dates. `dateModified` changes only when the content actually changed, never on a bare redeploy.
10. **CO-170 — Change triggers revalidation.** Any template or data-model change re-runs validation on every affected page type before release. A refactor that touches rendering is presumed to touch markup until validation proves otherwise.
11. **CO-171 — Monitored after deployment.** Search Console enhancement reports are reviewed on the web-analytics cadence. A new error or invalid-item class is a defect with a named owner, not a statistic to watch.
12. **CO-172 — Page-external fields verified, not exempt.** Fields with no visible counterpart by design (e.g. an organization's founding date or logo) are verified against fact-sheet.md before the template ships, and re-verified when the fact sheet changes.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-081 — Markup-only claims.** Banned: JSON-LD stating ratings, prices, dates, or authors the visible page never shows. Defeats: DET-CON-024. Instead: generate the block from the page's data (CO-161); if no reviews render, no rating markup ships (CO-166). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-082 — Generator placeholders in production.** Banned: shipping JSON-LD containing scaffold values such as "Product Name", `price: 0.00`, or `https://example.com/logo.png`. Defeats: DET-CON-003. Instead: bind every property to the page's data store and fail the build on placeholder patterns (CO-165, G-CO-083). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-083 — Fabricated review markup.** Banned: `aggregateRating` or `Review` markup without real, visible, attributable reviews behind it. Defeats: DET-CON-013. Instead: no real visible reviews, no review markup — route the reviews themselves through real-content first (CO-166). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-084 — Separately maintained markup copies.** Banned: static JSON-LD blocks stored apart from the page data and edited by hand, so markup and page drift apart over time. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: one template reads the same record the page renders (CO-161); price changes propagate in the same commit (CO-167). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-085 — Marking up hidden content.** Banned: describing in JSON-LD any content that is hidden from users on the page (display:none sections, unloaded tabs, geo-gated blocks). Defeats: DET-CON-024. Instead: mark up exactly the visible set; if a question matters, show it (CO-162). Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-081 — CI schema validation.** Verifies: CO-164, CO-168. Check: automated — on every build, fetch one sample URL per page type from the staging build, extract each `application/ld+json` block, parse it as JSON, and validate required properties per type against Google's rich-result requirements (Rich Results Test during development). Pass: every block parses and carries all required properties. Fail: block the build.
- **G-CO-082 — Markup-vs-visible diff.** Verifies: CO-162, CO-167, CO-169. Check: automated — script diffs `aggregateRating`, `price`, `datePublished`/`dateModified`, and `author` values in JSON-LD against the rendered page text for the same sample URLs. Pass: zero fields without an identical visible counterpart (page-external fields checked against fact-sheet.md per CO-172). Fail: block shipment; this gate runs the DET-CON-024 check.
- **G-CO-083 — Placeholder scan.** Verifies: CO-165. Check: automated — grep all emitted JSON-LD in the build output for `Product Name`, `example.com`, `example.org`, `"price": 0`, `Lorem`, and `TODO`. Pass: zero hits. Fail: block the build.
- **G-CO-084 — Change-triggered revalidation.** Verifies: CO-170. Check: manual with checklist — any merge touching a markup template or its data model lists the affected page types, and G-CO-081/G-CO-082 results for those types are attached to the change before release. Pass: revalidation evidence present for every affected type. Fail: hold the release.
- **G-CO-085 — Enhancement-report review.** Verifies: CO-171. Check: manual — on the web-analytics cadence, open Search Console's rich-result enhancement reports and log new error/invalid classes with a named owner and fix date. Pass: review logged for the current cycle with no unowned error class. Fail: escalate as a defect before the next release.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Every JSON-LD block is template-generated from the page's own data store (CO-161).
- [ ] Every markup field has an identical visible counterpart, or a fact-sheet entry (CO-162, CO-172).
- [ ] Required properties complete for each type's rich result (G-CO-081).
- [ ] Review/aggregateRating markup exists only over real, visible reviews (CO-166).
- [ ] Markup price equals page price equals checkout price (CO-167).
- [ ] Placeholder scan returns zero hits in the build output (G-CO-083).
- [ ] Markup-vs-visible diff passes on a sample URL per page type (G-CO-082).
- [ ] Template or data-model changes carry revalidation evidence (G-CO-084).

# technical-seo

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** none — standalone: it audits the site's own rendered output, server responses, and robots/sitemap files — the crawl-and-index contract is checked against the site itself, not another skill's output. It feeds on-page-seo, aeo, geo, sitemaps, and web-analytics.
- **Feeds into:** on-page-seo, aeo, geo, sitemaps, web-analytics

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a site is built, migrated, redesigned, or promoted between environments, and whenever crawlability, rendering, indexation, canonicalization, or redirect behavior is in question. This skill owns the crawl-and-index contract between the site and search engines.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is what a page says (copywriting, on-page-seo), what its markup declares (structured-data), or which URLs the sitemap lists (sitemaps — this skill sets the contract that skill generates against). Never use it to promise a ranking: Google documents eligibility requirements, not ranking outcomes.

## Rules

1. **CO-001 — The indexable-page contract.** Every page intended for search returns HTTP 200, carries a self-referencing canonical, and is reachable by following links from the site itself. A page failing any leg is a defect to fix, not a ranking mystery to explain.
2. **CO-002 — Server-rendered by default.** Indexable content ships as server-rendered or statically generated HTML. Client-side rendering of indexable content is an exception that must be verified under CO-003, never a default.
3. **CO-003 — Verify the rendered HTML.** JavaScript-dependent content is checked in the rendered HTML (Search Console URL Inspection or an equivalent rendered-DOM fetch), never assumed from source code, view-source, or a local build.
4. **CO-004 — robots.txt discipline.** robots.txt follows RFC 9309 syntax, is served at the host root with HTTP 200, and never blocks the CSS or JavaScript assets that rendering the pages requires. Every change to it is reviewed like a code change.
5. **CO-005 — The promotion indexability diff.** Before every production release, staging and production are diffed on robots.txt, `noindex` (meta and X-Robots-Tag), basic-auth walls, and canonical host. Any staging protection found in production is a release blocker.
6. **CO-006 — One canonical URL per page.** Each page has exactly one canonical URL, stated as an absolute URL that itself returns 200 and is indexable. Parameter, filter, sort, session, and print variants canonicalize to the base URL or carry `noindex`; they are never indexable duplicates competing with it.
7. **CO-007 — Redirect hygiene.** Permanent moves use 301 or 308. Redirects are single-hop wherever the destination is known; a chain longer than two hops is fixed at the source, not documented and left.
8. **CO-008 — Real status codes.** Missing content returns a real 404 or 410. An error page served with HTTP 200 (a soft 404) is a defect, as is redirecting every removed URL to the homepage.
9. **CO-009 — One host, one scheme.** The site canonicalizes to a single host form (www or non-www) over HTTPS. Every other host/scheme combination 301-redirects to it, and canonicals, sitemaps, and internal links use only that form.
10. **CO-010 — The sitemap contract.** The XML sitemap lists only canonical, indexable URLs that return 200, is regenerated when routes change, stays within protocol limits (50,000 URLs / 50 MB per file, sitemap index beyond that), and is referenced in robots.txt. Generation itself belongs to the sitemaps skill; this rule is the contract it must satisfy.
11. **CO-011 — Directive consistency.** robots.txt, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag, and canonicals never contradict each other on the same URL, and no CDN, firewall, or hosting rule blocks search or AI crawlers that robots.txt allows — Google names CDN/hosting-level blocking as a real eligibility failure for its AI features.
12. **CO-012 — Coverage reviewed on a cadence.** Search Console coverage and indexing reports are reviewed on a fixed cadence (monthly at minimum) and the review is logged. Every spike in excluded or error URLs is triaged to a named cause. Reports state eligibility and defects found; they never state or imply a ranking guarantee.

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-001 — Staging protection shipped live.** Banned: promoting a build whose production environment still carries staging `noindex`, `Disallow: /`, a basic-auth wall, or staging-host canonicals. Defeats: DET-CON-002. Instead: run the CO-005 promotion diff; production ships only when no staging directive survives. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-002 — Indexable duplicate URL variants.** Banned: letting parameter, filter, sort, or session URLs be indexed as separate pages with self-referencing canonicals, splitting signals across duplicates of one page. Defeats: DET-CON-025. Instead: variants canonicalize to the base URL or carry `noindex` (CO-006); only substantively different pages are indexable. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-003 — Soft 404s.** Banned: serving "page not found" content with HTTP 200, or answering every deleted URL with a redirect to the homepage. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: return a real 404/410 for gone content, and 301 only to a genuinely equivalent replacement (CO-008). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-004 — Ranking guarantees and fabricated visibility wins.** Banned: promising a ranking, traffic figure, or AI-citation outcome in any plan or report, or reporting an unadopted proposal (e.g. llms.txt, which Google states on the record it does not use) as an AI-visibility win. Defeats: DET-CON-026. Instead: report only what Google documents — indexed, snippet-eligible, defects fixed — and label every other claim with its evidence level or cut it. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-CO-001 — Promotion indexability diff.** Verifies: CO-005, CO-004, CO-011. Check: automated — script fetches staging and production robots.txt plus the response headers and meta robots of the top route templates, and diffs directives and canonical host. Pass: zero staging protections (noindex, Disallow: /, auth wall, staging canonical) present in production. Fail: block the release. Before a production environment is provisioned, this gate's disposition is a recorded provisioning waiver per the §6.3 protocol; it unblocks when a production environment is provisioned and the release is deployed to it.
- **G-CO-002 — Route inventory crawl.** Verifies: CO-001, CO-006, CO-009. Check: automated — crawl the production route inventory and assert, per indexable URL: HTTP 200, self-referencing canonical in the canonical host form, no `noindex`. Pass: 100% of indexable URLs satisfy all three. Fail: block shipment of the affected routes.
- **G-CO-003 — Redirect and status audit.** Verifies: CO-007, CO-008. Check: automated — follow every redirect reachable from internal links and the sitemap; assert chains are ≤2 hops, permanent moves are 301/308, and a sample of deleted URLs returns 404/410, not 200 or a homepage redirect. Pass: all assertions hold. Fail: fix at the source and re-run.
- **G-CO-004 — Rendered-content verification.** Verifies: CO-002, CO-003. Check: manual with tooling — for a sample of JavaScript-dependent templates, compare the rendered HTML (URL Inspection or rendered-DOM fetch) against the expected primary content: heading, body text, links, canonical. Pass: primary content fully present in the rendered HTML for every sampled template. Fail: treat as a rendering defect; do not ship the template.
- **G-CO-005 — Coverage review log.** Verifies: CO-012. Check: manual — the monthly Search Console review exists in the project log with excluded/error counts, each spike triaged to a named cause, and no ranking or traffic guarantee stated anywhere in it. Pass: log entry complete for the current month. Fail: the review is overdue; complete it before the next release.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Promotion indexability diff is clean: no staging directive in production (G-CO-001).
- [ ] Every indexable URL returns 200 with a self-referencing canonical (G-CO-002).
- [ ] robots.txt is RFC 9309-valid and blocks no render asset (CO-004).
- [ ] Redirect chains are ≤2 hops; permanent moves are 301/308 (G-CO-003).
- [ ] Deleted URLs return a real 404/410 — no soft 404s (CO-008).
- [ ] JavaScript-dependent templates verified in rendered HTML (G-CO-004).
- [ ] Sitemap lists only canonical, indexable, 200 URLs (CO-010).
- [ ] This month's Search Console coverage review is logged, with no ranking guarantee stated (G-CO-005).

# web-analytics

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D9 SEO & Content (CO)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** technical-seo, product-analytics (D12 — owner of the shared tracking plan)
- **Feeds into:** content-strategy, on-page-seo, growth-experiments

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** search and acquisition measurement is set up, audited, or reported: Search Console verification, coverage and performance review, GA4 organic landing-page analysis, and the content decisions that follow from them. This skill owns the search/acquisition slice of measurement.
- **Do NOT use when:** the question is product behavior inside the app — funnels, feature usage, retention — or the event taxonomy itself: those belong to D12 (product-analytics, event-tracking). **Boundary: one shared tracking plan, two consumers.** D12 owns the plan and the event names; this skill consumes them for search reporting and never invents, renames, or duplicates an event.

## Rules

1. **CO-241 — Search and acquisition only.** This skill measures how search and acquisition channels deliver visitors: Search Console performance (queries, pages, clicks, impressions), coverage/indexing, rich-result reports, and GA4 organic landing-page behavior. Anything past the landing page is D12's slice of the shared plan.
2. **CO-242 — Every production property verified.** Search Console is verified for every production property, including domain variants, and the GA4 property is linked. An unverified property is a blind spot and is treated as a defect with an owner, not an oversight.
3. **CO-243 — The tracking plan is the contract.** Every tag and event this skill relies on is an entry in the shared tracking plan (D12-owned): name, trigger, parameters, owner. A live tag with no plan entry, or a plan entry with no live implementation, is a defect found by the G-CO-121 diff.
4. **CO-244 — Configuration is verified, never assumed.** A pasted snippet proves nothing. Each relied-on event is observed firing — in GA4 DebugView or Tag Assistant — with the plan's exact name and parameters, and the primary conversion is completed end to end in a debug session before anyone reports on it.
5. **CO-245 — Consent is respected end to end.** Where consent mode applies, analytics does not collect before the visitor's consent state allows it, and the consent configuration is verified in a fresh, no-consent session — not inferred from the banner being visible on the page.
6. **CO-246 — Fixed review cadence.** Search Console coverage and performance are reviewed monthly at minimum, and the review is logged with the actions it produced. A review that produces no briefs, refreshes, retirements, or technical fixes — and says why — is an incomplete review.
7. **CO-247 — No content decision without a citation.** Every brief, refresh, and retirement this skill informs names the query, page, or landing-page evidence behind it. "We should write about X" with no Search Console or GA4 evidence cited does not enter content-strategy's queue.
8. **CO-248 — AI-feature traffic is read where Google reports it.** Appearances in Google's AI features are reported inside Search Console's overall Performance data. They are never split out, estimated, or presented as a separate metric — no platform publishes such a number, so any standalone "AI traffic" figure is invented.
9. **CO-249 — Every reported figure reproduces from source.** Each number in a report names its platform, property, report, date range, and filters, and can be re-pulled to the same value. A figure nobody can reproduce is cut from the report, not footnoted.
10. **CO-250 — Event and tag changes go through the plan.** Changes are proposed into the shared tracking plan, keep D12's names consistent, and are debug-validated before release. No duplicate or variant spellings of an existing event are ever shipped (BAN-CO-124).
11. **CO-251 — Indexing regressions are incidents.** A spike in excluded or error URLs, or a sudden drop in indexed pages, is triaged to a named cause with an owner and a fix or an accepted-risk note — never left as an observation on a chart.
12. **CO-252 — Reports are dated and current.** Every report states its pull date, date range, and comparison convention, and its figures come from that pull. A recycled screenshot or a figure from a previous period presented as current is stale copy (BAN-CO-125).

## BAN list

- **BAN-CO-121 — Invented metrics reported as measured.** Banned: presenting any metric no platform produces — a standalone "AI Overview traffic" number, a paid "GEO score" shown as a platform metric, an estimated citation share — as measured fact in a plan or report. Defeats: DET-CON-011. Instead: report AI-feature appearances only inside overall Performance data (CO-248); label anything else with its evidence level or cut it. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-122 — Measurement claimed, never configured.** Banned: announcing that analytics or conversion tracking is "set up" when the snippet is pasted but no tracking-plan entry exists and no debug session has ever verified an event firing. Defeats: DET-CON-028. Instead: no measurement claim until the G-CO-121 plan diff is clean and a G-CO-122 debug session has completed the primary conversion. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-123 — Consent promise without the configuration.** Banned: privacy or consent copy stating that tracking starts only after consent, while tags fire on page load regardless of consent state. Defeats: DET-CON-015. Instead: make the firing match the promise — consent state gates collection (CO-245) and the fresh-session check in G-CO-122 proves it. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-124 — Duplicate and misspelled event variants.** Banned: shipping variant spellings of one event (`sign_up`, `signup`, `SignUp`) so a single action fragments across several report rows. Defeats: DET-CON-017. Instead: one canonical name from the shared tracking plan (CO-250); variants are removed and the change is debug-validated before release. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-CO-125 — Stale figures presented as current.** Banned: reusing a previous period's screenshot, export, or headline number in a current report, including after the underlying tag has broken. Defeats: DET-CON-018. Instead: every report is built from a fresh, dated pull (CO-252), and a broken tag is a CO-251 incident, not a quiet gap. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-CO-121 — Tracking-plan diff.** Verifies: CO-243, CO-250. Check: automated — export the live tag/event list (GTM container export or a crawl grep for measurement IDs, e.g. `grep -rhoE "G-[A-Z0-9]{6,}" dist/ | sort -u`, plus the implemented event names) and diff it against the shared tracking plan's entries. Pass: zero live tags or events missing from the plan, and zero plan entries with no live implementation. Fail: block the release until the diff is clean.
- **G-CO-122 — DebugView conversion and consent session.** Verifies: CO-244, CO-245. Check: manual with tooling — in a fresh browser profile, load the site with no consent given and confirm no analytics collection beyond consent-state pings; then grant consent, complete the primary conversion flow, and watch GA4 DebugView. Pass: the conversion event fires exactly once, under its plan name with its plan parameters, and nothing collected before consent. Fail: block; fix configuration and re-run.
- **G-CO-123 — Monthly Search Console review.** Verifies: CO-242, CO-246, CO-251. Check: manual — the review log holds an entry for the current month covering every verified property: coverage counts, performance summary, each exclusion or error spike triaged to a named cause and owner, and the actions the review produced. Pass: entry complete for the current month. Fail: the review is overdue; complete it before the next release.
- **G-CO-124 — Report reproducibility audit.** Verifies: CO-247, CO-248, CO-249, CO-252. Check: semi-automated — list every figure in the latest report; each must cite platform, property, report, and date range; re-pull a sample of at least two figures and compare values; scan the report for any standalone AI-feature metric. Pass: every sampled figure reproduces exactly and no invented metric appears. Fail: withdraw and reissue the report.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Search Console verified for every production property and domain variant (CO-242).
- [ ] Tracking-plan diff is clean: no live tag or event missing from the plan (G-CO-121).
- [ ] DebugView session completed the primary conversion exactly once, under its plan name (G-CO-122).
- [ ] Fresh no-consent session collects nothing before consent (CO-245).
- [ ] This month's Search Console coverage and performance review is logged, spikes triaged (G-CO-123).
- [ ] Every figure in the latest report reproduces from its cited source (G-CO-124).
- [ ] No standalone "AI traffic" or other invented metric appears in any report (CO-248).
